phase: 32 — validation of MCQ LINK_EXCLUDE behaviour before any fix (REVIEW ONLY, nothing modified)
verdictHeadline: INTENDED EXCLUSION: PROVEN. ROOT CAUSE: NOT PROVEN. Per the brief’s own gate ("If unclear, stop before proposing a production fix"), NO fix is proposed and no candidate was simulated.

evidence: chapter-app.js:2817 carries the explicit comment "Never linkify inside these (already interactive or would double-wrap)."

chapter-app.js:2818 LINK_EXCLUDE = button,a,summary,input,textarea,.word-pop,.builder-token,.builder-slot,.mcq-options,.quiz-stage,.reading-passage,.rw,.de-link,[data-no-link] — .mcq-options is named explicitly, AND the generic element selector "button" is the very first entry, so an mcq option is excluded twice over (mcq options are <button class="mcq-option">, chapter-app.js:3047 and :3346)
the neighbouring exclusions demonstrably work in the same rendered page: .quiz-stage 0 de-links, .builder-token/.builder-slot 0, .reading-passage 0
both linkifiers consult the same list: linkifyDe at :2826 and linkifyGated at :2906, each via elDe.closest(LINK_EXCLUDE)

the intent is coherent with the widget design — mcq options are themselves click targets (b.addEventListener('click') at :3051/:3350), so per-word popups inside them would fight the option button for the tap
step1_intendedBehaviour.conclusion: German text inside mcq options is intended NOT to be word-linkified. This is deliberate, redundantly specified, and effective everywhere else in the same list.

sequenceRead: chapter-app.js:3047-3049 const b = el('button', { class: 'mcq-option', type: 'button' }, el('span',{class:'mcq-key'}, …), el('span', { html: optionIsGerman(opt) ? ''+opt+'' : opt })) — the .de is created as a CHILD of the button in the same synchronous el() call, so it is inside button.mcq-option from the moment the button exists
chapter-app.js:3051 option click handler bound to the button
chapter-app.js:3423/3543 linkifyDe(host) + linkifyGated(host) run on an ATTACHED host after all blocks are appended
step2_domLifecycle.detachedSubtreeHypothesis: DISPROVEN. Two independent reasons: (a) el() nests the .de inside the button synchronously, so there is no window in which the .de exists without a button ancestor; (b) live inspection confirms every mcq .de is currently attached with closest(LINK_EXCLUDE) === BUTTON.mcq-option, so a linkifier running now would correctly skip it. Phase 31 recorded this hypothesis as STRONGLY SUPPORTED; that grading was wrong and is retracted here.
step2_domLifecycle.whereTheAncestorRelationshipIsMissing: NOWHERE — the ancestor relationship is present. The exclusion is not failing because of the DOM shape.

step2b_decisiveNegativeEvidence.observation: in the rendered b2-15, 30 .de-link nodes exist inside .mcq-options (5 host .de elements), yet NONE of those 5 host .de elements carries any dataset key at all — no data-linked (set by linkifyDe at :2827) and no data-linked-gated (set by linkifyGated at :2907)
step2b_decisiveNegativeEvidence.inference: neither known linkifier processed these elements — both stamp their marker BEFORE wrapping, so a processed host always carries one. The .de-link spans inside mcq options are therefore produced by a THIRD, unidentified code path that does not consult LINK_EXCLUDE.
step2b_decisiveNegativeEvidence.confidence: PROVEN that neither linkifyDe nor linkifyGated processed them; the identity of the actual producer is NOT established
step2b_decisiveNegativeEvidence.alsoNotable: document-wide, 30 of 30 .de-link nodes inside any <button> are exactly these mcq ones — no other button type is breached

step3_candidates.assessmentBlocked: every candidate in the brief presumes the breach comes from linkifyDe’s ancestor test. That presumption is now disproven, so all four would be fixes to the wrong site.
step3_candidates.A_attachBeforeLinkify: INEFFECTIVE — the subtree is already attached and already inside a button; attachment order is not the variable
step3_candidates.B_passHostIntoLinkifyDe: INEFFECTIVE — same reason; closest() already resolves to BUTTON.mcq-option
step3_candidates.C_mcqGuardAtCallSite: INEFFECTIVE against the real producer — linkifyDe/linkifyGated are not creating these nodes
step3_candidates.D_smallestArchitectureCompatible: CANNOT BE IDENTIFIED until the producing code path is found. The correct next step is to locate the third linkification path (candidates to inspect: any MutationObserver-driven sweep, any wrapWordsIn/story-token path invoked on exercise content, or a re-render that rebuilds option innerHTML from already-linkified markup).

step4_simulatedFixRegression.reason: simulating a patch to linkifyDe or linkifyGated would prove nothing: those functions did not create the 14 links. A harness patch would leave all 14 in place and produce a misleading "fix does not work" result, or worse, a misleading pass. Refused deliberately rather than reported as evidence.

whatWasVerifiedInstead.mcqBreachScope: 30 de-links across 5 host .de elements in b2-15 alone
whatWasVerifiedInstead.normalTokensUnaffected: 718 .de-link total in b2-15, i.e. the overwhelming majority are legitimate story/reading/grammar/vocabulary links outside any excluded region

step5_mcqInteraction.optionSelection: unaffected by any exclusion change — the handler is bound to the button itself (chapter-app.js:3051, :3350), not to inner word spans
step5_mcqInteraction.answerChecking: unaffected — b.classList.add(is-correct/is-wrong) and the disable sweep $$('.mcq-option', opts).forEach(x => x.disabled = true) operate on the button (:3053-3056, :3352-3355)
step5_mcqInteraction.keyboardInteraction: unaffected — <button type="button"> keeps native focus/Enter/Space semantics; removing inner spans does not change tab order
step5_mcqInteraction.caveat: today the inner word spans ARE clickable inside a disabled-able button, which means a learner can currently tap a word inside a distractor option. Removing that restores the intended single tap target. No regression to option behaviour is expected from removing inner linkification.

step7_recommendation.A_intendedMcqBehaviour: PROVEN: mcq option text must not be word-linkified (comment + double exclusion + effective sibling exclusions + option-button click design)
step7_recommendation.B_provenRootCause: NOT PROVEN. Proven negatives only: the DOM ancestry is correct, both known linkifiers check LINK_EXCLUDE, and neither processed these hosts (no dataset marker). An unidentified third path creates the links.
step7_recommendation.C_candidateFixes: all four brief candidates are invalidated by the negative evidence; none is recommended
step7_recommendation.D_recommendedSmallestFix: NONE YET — stop, per the brief’s gate. Next phase should identify the producing code path, not patch a presumed one.
step7_recommendation.E_diagnosticResults: exclusion effective for quiz-stage/builder/reading-passage (0 each); breached only for mcq options (30 nodes in b2-15); host .de elements carry no linkifier marker
step7_recommendation.F_expectedReduction: still 14 HCM and 11 RCB if mcq option text stops being linkified — unchanged from Phase 31, since the target set is unchanged
step7_recommendation.G_regressionRisks: unquantifiable until the producer is known. If the producer turns out to be a re-render path, the fix may also affect other re-rendered regions.
step7_recommendation.H_filesThatWouldChange: UNKNOWN — cannot be named without the producing path. It will be somewhere in chapter/chapter-app.js; no chapter data, CSS, or QA file is implicated.

correctionsToEarlierPhases: Phase 31 graded the detached-subtree explanation STRONGLY SUPPORTED. It is now DISPROVEN. The finding that all 14 sit inside button.mcq-option and that .mcq-options is in LINK_EXCLUDE still stands — only the mechanism was wrong.
